html:
The Ngombur were an Aboriginal Australian people of the far north of the Northern Territory, on the map near the Alligator Rivers, in the country of today's Kakadu National Park.

Almost nothing is recorded about them, and their language is long extinct. Their neighbours on the map are the Gaagudju, Limilngan, Wuningangk and Warray. The peoples of this floodplain country lived from the wetlands, rich in geese, fish and turtles, and left a long record of rock art.
sum: The Ngombur were an Aboriginal Australian people of the far north of the Northern Territory, on the map near the Alligator Rivers, in the country of today's Kakadu National Park.
